units.title: The actual weak resolvent admits C1 compact weighted tests

sources.label: PBPS Appendix C.1 omitted analytic domain prerequisite
sources.scope: Same actual compact-gradient graph closure admits C1 compact function/gradient pairs; actual positive-epsilon weak resolvent has all C1 compact weighted volume tests and genuine ordinary weak gradient. Actual PBPS reflected conditional R/S law and original fixed D precede epsilon/input. No local H2, global operator-core/Bochner, conditional Poincare/BL, centered epsilon limit, noncompact constant/linear domains, measurable y-selection, SPHMC Hessian lower/full4.1, PBPS hypocoercivity or either complete main/composition. TV never transfers unbounded expected cost.

assumptions: E has the same finite-dimensional real Hilbert/Borel/full-space structure, including dimension zero. W is C1 and exp(-W) is genuinely integrable for volume. The law mu is exactly volume.tilted(-W), whose probability normalization is derived.

D is the same closable partial gradient with exact compact smooth representative graph. epsilon is positive and forcing f is a genuine scalar L2(mu) class. No weak solution, H1 membership of a test, differentiability of u, coercivity or Poincare certificate is supplied.

All quantifiers/representatives/measures are retained: the weak equation tests every original closure-domain element; ordinary weak derivatives use volume and every C1 compact scalar test/direction; the weighted equation now uses every C1 compact scalar test, with all three products L1 for volume.
units.statement: For C1 W and genuine integrability of exp(-W) volume, let mu=volume.tilted(-W). For every same closable exact compact smooth gradient D, epsilon>0 and scalar L2(mu) input f, construct u in D.closure.domain satisfying the variational equation for every domain test. Its actual closed gradient is the ordinary weak gradient, with locally volume-integrable representatives and full C1 compact directional identities. For every C1 compact psi, all three weighted volume products are integrable and epsilon integral exp(-W)u psi + integral exp(-W)<D.closure u,gradient psi> = integral exp(-W)f psi.
units.boundary: Same actual compact-gradient graph closure admits C1 compact function/gradient pairs; actual positive-epsilon weak resolvent has all C1 compact weighted volume tests and genuine ordinary weak gradient. steps.title: Construct the same genuine variational solution
steps.text: Positive epsilon and the actual closed partial operator give the true weak solution on D.closure.domain. The same D precedes epsilon and input; no Poisson solvability or Poincare premise is inserted.

steps.title: Retain the ordinary weak gradient and representatives
steps.text: The existing exact graph/distributional producer gives local volume integrability and every C1 compact directional weak-gradient identity for the very same u and D.closure u.

steps.title: Embed each actual C1 compact test in this domain
steps.text: Use the newly proved joint domain producer, yielding true MemLp classes p=[psi],q=[gradient psi] and their pair in this same closure graph. Extract the domain element v with D.closure v=q.

steps.title: Derive integrability before integral algebra
steps.text: Actual L2 inner integrability gives the three mu-products. The proved tilted-law integrability equivalence transfers them to exp(-W)-weighted volume. No integral of an unproved nonintegrable expression is rearranged.

steps.title: Remove only the true positive normalization
steps.text: Rewrite the actual L2 inner products with their mu-a.e. representatives and true tilted integrals. Cancel the reciprocal of the genuine positive partition to obtain the weighted volume equation for every C1 compact psi.

steps.title: Permit legitimate inverseweight tests without higher-regularity claims
steps.text: For smooth compact phi, exp(W)phi is still compact and C1 when W is C1, so the new class is the needed legitimate input. This theorem does not itself establish the ordinary Laplacian, local H2, global Bochner or BL.
steps.formula: e^W\phi\in C_c^1;\quad\text{higher operator-domain conclusions remain separate}.
